npc-civil-registration-page.title: Civil Registration — National Population Commission

npc-civil-registration-page.notes: Publicly accessible official NPC webpage (HTTP 200 on 31 October 2026). Establishes that the Births, Deaths, Etc. npc-faqs-page.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) — National Population Commission
npc-faqs-page.documentReference: Official NPC FAQ sections: Getting Started, Birth Registration (Ages 0–17), Birth Attestation (Ages 18+), Re-issuance (Pre-November 2023 Certificates), Certificate Reprint, Modify Record, and Support (support@vitalreg.org)
npc-faqs-page.notes: Publicly accessible official NPC FAQ page (HTTP 200 on 31 October 2026). Explicitly establishes: (1) Account creation on the VitalReg Self-Service Portal requires being 18+ with a valid NIN and facial verification; (2) Birth Registration on the self-service portal covers individuals aged 0 to 17 years where at least one parent is Nigerian and holds a valid Birth Certificate or Attestation Number; (3) Center-based birth registration can proceed without a child NIN if the parent/guardian provides a valid NIN; (4) Birth Attestation covers individuals aged 18 years and above with NIN and a Court Sworn Affidavit; (5) Re-issuance upgrades non-digital birth or attestation certificates issued before November 2023; (6) Approved digital certificates can be downloaded once free of additional charge, while additional copies require a paid Certificate Reprint request; (7) Approved digital records can be modified via Modify Record. Does not publish numeric NGN fee figures directly in the public FAQ text.

services.name: Birth registration and e-birth certificate for child under 5 at NPC registration centre
services.jurisdiction: Federal (Nationwide across 36 States, FCT and 774 LGAs)
services.description: In-person registration of a live birth and issuance of a digital e-Birth Certificate (integrated with NIMC National Identification Number where enrolled) for a child under the age of 5 years at any of the over 4,000 National Population Commission (NPC) registration centres and partnered Primary Health Centres nationwide.
services.eligibilityAndScope: Children aged 0 to under 5 years born in Nigeria, presented by an eligible informant under Section 10 of the Births, Deaths, Etc. (Compulsory Registration) Act 1992 (mother or father; or in their default, the occupier of the house/person in charge of the health institution, a person present at the birth, or the person having charge of the child).
services.ageAndTimingConditions: Applies to children under 5 years of age at physical NPC registration centres. Under the Compulsory Registration Act, births occurring in a health institution or house should be registered promptly (statutorily within 60 days of birth), and NPC explicitly provides free registration at every NPC registration centre for children under 5 years.
services.responsibleBody: National Population Commission (NPC) — Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (CRVS) Department, operating in collaboration with the National Primary Health Care Development Agency (NPHCDA) and NIMC.
services.deliveryChannelSummary: In-person visit to an accredited NPC Registration Centre (located in Primary Health Centres, general hospitals, LGA headquarters and NPC State/FCT offices). No online payment is required for centre-based under-5 registration.
services.processingStandard: Not stated as a fixed national SLA turnaround across all centres; in equipped digital eCRVS/hospital centres (such as the newborn registration drives documented by NPC), the digital e-birth certificate is issued immediately upon capture and verification.
requirements: Valid National Identification Number (NIN) of the parent, guardian or informant (NPC FAQs confirm registration can proceed without a child NIN at an NPC registration centre provided the parent or guardian supplies a valid NIN).
Child’s National Identification Number (NIN) if already enrolled, or newborn/child demographic particulars for integrated NIN + e-birth registration.
Evidence of birth from the hospital, maternity home or health facility (such as hospital birth notification / immunization card) where the birth occurred in a health institution.
Full particulars of the child (full name, sex, date of birth, place/town/LGA/state of birth, birth order and birth type).
Full particulars of the mother and father (full names, dates of birth/ages, states of origin, nationalities, marital status, educational levels and occupations).
Contact details and relationship of the informant if someone other than the parents is registering the birth.
processSteps: Locate the nearest NPC Registration Centre at a Primary Health Centre, public hospital, Local Government Area (LGA) secretariat or NPC State/FCT office (https://nationalpopulation.gov.ng/our-offices).
Present the child, parent/guardian NIN, and hospital birth record or delivery particulars to the authorised NPC Birth Registrar (in-person stage).
The NPC Registrar captures the child’s and parents’ particulars on the NPC Electronic Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (eCRVS) system and links or initiates the child’s NIN record.
Receive the official NPC e-Birth Certificate at no cost (do not pay informal fees to third-party touts for under-5 registration at an NPC registration centre).
services.notes: Substantiated as free by two independent official NPC sources: (1) Official NPC Statement dated 1 January 2025 (https://nationalpopulation.gov.ng/news/first-lady-welcomes-and-presents-birth-certificate-to-first-baby-of-the-year-2025) stating that the digital e-birth certificate with NIN "is entirely free" across over 4,000 registration centres; and (2) the VitalReg Self-Service Portal requirement notice (https://vitalreg-selfservice.nationalpopulation.gov.ng/, config fF) stating: "Birth registrations for children under the age of 5 years are free at every NPC registration center."
services.paymentGuide: Centre-based birth registration for a child under 5 years is officially published by NPC as free (₦0) at every NPC registration centre. Attend an accredited NPC registration centre or partnered Primary Health Centre in person; do not pay intermediaries.

services.name: Centre-based late birth registration (ages 5 to 17 years) and special registrar-assisted birth categories
services.jurisdiction: Federal (Nationwide across 36 States, FCT and 774 LGAs)
services.description: In-person birth registration at an NPC Registration Centre or State/LGA office for children and minors aged 5 to 17 years (beyond the free under-5 centre window) and registrar-assisted special birth registration pathways (adopted child, surrogate birth, and single-parent birth registration) on the NPC eCRVS Registrar Portal.
services.eligibilityAndScope: Children and young persons aged 5 to 17 years born in Nigeria whose births were not registered before age 5, as well as parents/legal guardians registering an adopted child, a child born through surrogacy, or a single-parent birth through an authorised NPC Registrar.
services.ageAndTimingConditions: NPC FAQs (/FAQs and /faq-vitalreg) define Birth Registration as covering ages 0 to 17 years (with ages 18 and above requiring Birth Attestation). While under-5 registration at NPC centres is explicitly published as free, NPC does not state that ages 5–17 at physical centres are free.
services.responsibleBody: National Population Commission (NPC) — Authorised Birth Registrars, Deputy Chief Registrars (DCRs) and State Directors operating via https://ecrvs.nationalpopulation.gov.ng/.
services.deliveryChannelSummary: In-person visit to an NPC Registration Centre, LGA Vital Registration Office or NPC State/FCT Office for registrar capture and DCR approval on the eCRVS Registrar Portal.
services.processingStandard: Not stated on public NPC pages; requires registrar capture and DCR/State Office approval on the eCRVS platform.
requirements: Valid National Identification Number (NIN) of the parent(s) or legal guardian and (where required) the child.
Hospital birth record, immunization card, school record or other supporting proof of birth details for late registration (ages 5–17).
For Adopted Child Birth Registration: Official Adoption Order / Court Order and foster/adoptive parents’ NINs and supporting identification.
For Surrogate Birth Registration: Surrogacy Agreement / Medical Certificate of Birth and commissioning parents’ NINs and supporting identification.
For Single-Parent Birth Registration: Single parent’s NIN, valid Birth Certificate or Attestation Number, and supporting proof of birth.
processSteps: Visit an NPC State/FCT Office or LGA Registration Centre in person (https://nationalpopulation.gov.ng/our-offices).
Present the child’s and parents’ NINs and supporting birth, adoption or surrogacy documents to an authorised NPC Registrar.
Where a payment is generated on the eCRVS system, pay only against the official payment invoice/reference generated on the NPC eCRVS platform.
Await Deputy Chief Registrar (DCR) / State Director verification and approval, then collect or download the digital NPC Birth Certificate.
services.notes: Distinguishes free under-5 centre registration from late (ages 5–17) and special registrar-assisted categories. Public NPC pages do not publish a fee schedule for centre-based registration of children aged 5–17 years (recorded as unknown/pending, never assumed free). For special registrar categories on eCRVS (https://ecrvs.nationalpopulation.gov.ng/), the live eCRVS API (ecrvs-api.verxid.site) returns ₦20,000 for Adopted Child Registration, ₦10,000 for Surrogate Birth Registration, and ₦5,000 for Single-Parent Birth Registration; because these amounts are not published on a public NPC tariff page, they remain pending.
services.paymentGuide: Confirm the applicable official eCRVS invoice at an NPC State or LGA Registration Office before paying. Do not assume late registration (ages 5–17) is free, and pay only through official NPC eCRVS payment channels.

services.name: Online self-service birth registration (ages 0 to 17 years — VitalReg Portal)
services.description: Online self-service birth registration and digital e-Birth Certificate application for children and minors aged 0 to 17 years via the unified NPC VitalReg Self-Service Portal, including standard registration with a child NIN and temporary birth notification for children awaiting NIN enrolment.
services.eligibilityAndScope: Individuals aged 0 to 17 years born in Nigeria where at least one parent is Nigerian and holds a valid NPC Birth Certificate or Parent Attestation Number. The parent/informant creating the VitalReg self-service account must be 18 years or older with a valid NIN and facial verification.
services.ageAndTimingConditions: Available for registrants aged 0 to 17 years on the VitalReg Self-Service Portal. Note: while children under 5 can be registered free in person at an NPC registration centre, choosing the online self-service portal attracts the VitalReg portal service charge.
services.responsibleBody: National Population Commission (NPC) — VitalReg Electronic Civil Registration Self-Service Platform.
services.deliveryChannelSummary: 100% online application, NIN validation, facial verification and payment via https://vitalreg-selfservice.nationalpopulation.gov.ng/, followed by Deputy Chief Registrar (DCR) digital approval and single free certificate download on the portal (or in-person NIMC visit if using the Temporary Birth Notification without NIN pathway).
services.processingStandard: Not stated as a fixed hour/day guarantee on public NPC pages; certificate download becomes available on the VitalReg dashboard once the DCR approves the application and displays "Approved".

services.name: Death registration (Death Notification) and Death Certificate
services.jurisdiction: Federal (Nationwide across 36 States, FCT and 774 LGAs)
services.description: Official registration of a death occurring in Nigeria and issuance of an NPC Death Certificate (via an NPC Registration Centre or the VitalReg Self-Service Portal Death Notification module).
services.eligibilityAndScope: Registration of any death occurring in Nigeria (in a hospital/medical facility, maternity home, house, road side, aeroplane, ship, or other location) by an eligible informant under the Births, Deaths, Etc. (Compulsory Registration) Act 1992 (relatives present at death or in attendance during last illness, occupier of premises, or person arranging burial/cremation).
services.ageAndTimingConditions: Applies to deaths of persons of any age occurring in Nigeria. Under the Compulsory Registration Act, deaths are required to be registered promptly with the local registrar.
services.responsibleBody: National Population Commission (NPC) — Civil Registration Department, VitalReg Portal and LGA/Hospital Registrars.
services.deliveryChannelSummary: Available online via the VitalReg Self-Service Portal (/death-notification/requirements) or in person at an NPC Registration Centre. Supporting medical, court or police evidence depends on the place and circumstances of death.
services.processingStandard: Not stated on public NPC pages; requires DCR verification of the uploaded cause-of-death or corroborating evidence before certificate download/issuance.
requirements: Valid National Identification Number (NIN) of the informant and (where available) the deceased.

Particulars of the deceased (full name, sex, date of birth/age at death, marital status, occupation, state/LGA of origin and residential address) and particulars of death (date of death, place of death, town/state/LGA of death, and certified cause of death).
Mandatory supporting document based on place of death (configured in VitalReg options.helper):
• Hospital / Medical Facility or Maternity Home death: Medical Certificate of Cause of Death issued by a registered medical practitioner.
• Home death: Medical Certificate of Death OR High Court Affidavit of Death OR Community Leader Endorsement Letter (plus Deceased ID Card where available).
• Road-side / Crash death: Police Report AND Medical Certificate of Death.
• Aeroplane / Ship death: Official Incident Report AND Medical Certificate of Death.
processSteps: Obtain the required primary evidence of death from the relevant institution (e.g., Medical Certificate of Cause of Death from the hospital, Police Report for a road crash, or High Court Affidavit for an unattended home death).
Visit an NPC Registration Centre in person OR sign in to https://vitalreg-selfservice.nationalpopulation.gov.ng/ and select "Death Notification".
Validate the informant’s NIN, enter the deceased’s demographic particulars and the date, place and cause of death, and upload the required supporting document(s).
Submit the application at no NPC fee ("Death Registration is free") and collect or download the NPC Death Certificate once verified and approved by the DCR.
services.notes: In the live VitalReg Self-Service Portal frontend bundle (index-XX1KC8SJ.js, requirement object SF for /death-notification/requirements), NPC explicitly sets isFreeService: true and reqFeeText: "Death Registration is free". However, third-party documents required to prove the death (hospital medical certificate, police extract, or court affidavit) may carry separate hospital, police or court charges outside NPC.

services.eligibilityAndScope: Holders (or parents/informants) of an approved digitalized record on VitalReg ("Ensure your certificate is digitalized and approved" — NPC FAQs). Note: holders of pre-November 2023 paper certificates must first complete Digital Certificate Re-issuance before modifying fields, and changing an adult’s name by Deed Poll uses the separate Deed Poll module.

Updating a temporary birth record solely to attach a newly issued child NIN ("Update Record with NIN") is free.
services.responsibleBody: National Population Commission (NPC) — VitalReg Self-Service Portal and Deputy Chief Registrars (DCRs).
services.deliveryChannelSummary: Online submission, supporting document upload and payment via https://vitalreg-selfservice.nationalpopulation.gov.ng/ ("Modify Record" module), followed by DCR review and approval.

requirements: Existing approved digitalized NPC certificate or temporary notification record on VitalReg.
Valid National Identification Number (NIN) matching the modified details where applicable.
Selection of the specific field(s) to modify (e.g., Applicant Name, Sex, Face/Photo, Place of Birth, State/LGA of Birth, Father/Mother Details, or Date of Birth) and a valid reason for modification.
Supporting documentary evidence for the requested correction (such as Court Sworn Affidavit, Marriage Certificate, Newspaper Publication, Medical Certificate of Birth/Death, or NIMC slip).
processSteps: Log in to https://vitalreg-selfservice.nationalpopulation.gov.ng/ and ensure the target certificate is digitalized and shows "Approved" on your dashboard.
Navigate to the "Modify Record" module, select the certificate type (Birth Registration, Birth Attestation, Foreign Birth Notification, or Death Notification) and enter the Certificate ID.
Select the specific field(s) to be corrected, enter the corrected information, and upload the required supporting documents.

Pay the applicable modification fee generated by the portal (₦3,000 for standard birth or attestation field modifications, ₦35,000 if Date of Birth is selected, ₦2,000 for foreign birth notification modification, or ₦10,000 for death notification modification).
Await DCR review and approval on the VitalReg dashboard, then download the updated digital certificate.

services.name: Change of Name or Correction of Name by Deed Poll (VitalReg Deed Poll Module)
services.category: Civil Registration — Deed Poll & Name Change
services.description: Official recording and endorsement of a legal Change of Name (by Marriage or Other Reasons) or Correction of Name by Deed Poll against an existing digital NPC Birth Certificate or Birth Attestation Certificate on the VitalReg Self-Service Portal.
services.eligibilityAndScope: Adults who hold an approved digital NPC Birth Certificate or Birth Attestation Certificate on their VitalReg profile and wish to legally change or correct their registered name via an executed Deed Poll agreement.
services.ageAndTimingConditions: Requires an existing approved digital Birth Certificate or Birth Attestation on the applicant’s VitalReg profile. For "Name Change — Others" and "Name Correction", the live VitalReg pathway endpoint (/deed-poll/pathways) marks the base ₦50,000 fee as escalates: true (subject to certificate-based calculation via /payments/price/{pathway}?certificateIdentifier=...).
services.responsibleBody: National Population Commission (NPC) — VitalReg Deed Poll Module, working alongside Legal Practitioners and Courts.
services.deliveryChannelSummary: Online submission and payment via https://vitalreg-selfservice.nationalpopulation.gov.ng/ (/deed-poll), using either the "Self-Service" route (applicant engages their own lawyer to prepare and execute the Deed Poll) or the "Accredited Legal Practitioner" route (selecting an NPC-licensed law firm on the portal).
services.processingStandard: Not stated on public NPC pages; requires online submission, payment and NPC legal/DCR review.
requirements: Existing approved digital NPC Birth Certificate or Birth Attestation Certificate on the applicant’s VitalReg profile.
Valid National Identification Number (NIN) matching the new/corrected name (or updated NIN slip).
Executed Deed Poll Agreement prepared by a qualified legal practitioner.
Sworn Court Affidavit of Change/Correction of Name.
Newspaper Publication of the change of name (or Marriage Certificate / supporting legal evidence for Name Change by Marriage).
Recent digital passport photograph and valid government-issued ID.
processSteps: Ensure your NPC Birth Certificate or Birth Attestation Certificate is digitalized and shows "Approved" on https://vitalreg-selfservice.nationalpopulation.gov.ng/.
Select "Deed Poll" on the VitalReg portal and choose either "Self-Service" (using your own legal practitioner) or "Accredited Legal Practitioner" (selecting an NPC-accredited law firm).
Select your existing Birth Certificate or Birth Attestation record and choose the applicable Deed Poll pathway: "Name Change by Marriage", "Name Change — Others", or "Name Correction".
Upload the executed Deed Poll agreement, court affidavit, newspaper publication / marriage certificate, and supporting identification.
Pay the official VitalReg Deed Poll fee online and await NPC approval to download your Deed Poll endorsement / updated certificate.
services.notes: Discovered in the live VitalReg bundle (chunk deed-poll.q-DTuFytgi.js) and verified against the live unauthenticated pathway endpoint (https://ecrvs-api.verxid.site/deed-poll/pathways and /payments/price/*). Note that private legal practitioner fees for drafting the Deed Poll, court affidavit fees, and newspaper publication fees are separate third-party charges outside NPC’s portal fee.

services.name: Stillbirth Registration (Compulsory Civil Registration)
services.jurisdiction: Federal (Nationwide across 36 States, FCT and 774 LGAs)
services.description: Statutory civil registration of a stillbirth (a child born after the 28th week of pregnancy that did not breathe or show any other sign of life after complete separation from the mother) at an NPC Registration Centre under the Births, Deaths, Etc. (Compulsory Registration) Act 1992.
services.eligibilityAndScope: Parents, relatives or health-institution officers reporting a stillbirth occurring in Nigeria under the Births, Deaths, Etc. (Compulsory Registration) Act, Act No. 69 of 1992.
services.ageAndTimingConditions: Applies to foetal deaths occurring after 28 weeks of gestation as defined on NPC’s Civil Registration page.
services.responsibleBody: National Population Commission (NPC) — Authorised Registrars at health facilities and LGA registration centres (via https://ecrvs.nationalpopulation.gov.ng/ /dashboard/still-births).
services.deliveryChannelSummary: In-person registration by an authorised NPC Registrar at the hospital/health institution or LGA NPC Registration Centre.
services.processingStandard: Not stated on public NPC pages.
requirements: Medical Certificate of Stillbirth signed by the attending registered medical practitioner or midwife (stating that the child was not born alive and the probable cause of foetal death), or informant declaration where no medical practitioner/midwife was present.
Valid National Identification Number (NIN) and particulars of the parent(s) / informant.
Particulars of the stillbirth (date and place of delivery, sex, gestational age/weight, and mother’s pregnancy/delivery details).
processSteps: Obtain the Medical Certificate of Stillbirth from the attending doctor or midwife at the health facility.
Present the certificate and parents’ details to the NPC Registrar assigned to the health facility or nearest NPC Registration Centre (https://nationalpopulation.gov.ng/our-offices).
The NPC Registrar records the event in the Stillbirth Register on the eCRVS platform (/dashboard/still-births) and issues the statutory acknowledgement/extract as applicable.
services.notes: Explicitly documented on NPC’s public Civil Registration page (https://nationalpopulation.gov.ng/civil-registration under "Stillbirth") and supported as a dedicated module (/dashboard/still-births) on the eCRVS Registrar Portal (https://ecrvs.nationalpopulation.gov.ng/). Neither the public NPC website nor the eCRVS price API publishes a fee for stillbirth registration; in accordance with FeeLens rules, a missing fee is recorded as unknown/pending and never assumed free.
services.paymentGuide: Register stillbirths in person through an authorised NPC Registrar at the health facility or nearest NPC office. Confirm whether any statutory extract charge applies; no fee is stated on public NPC pages.
